fields.Front: List the seven properties of relations.
fields.Back: Unique relation name; each cell holds one atomic value (1NF); unique attribute names within a table; values of an attribute come from the same domain; attribute order has no significance; each tuple is distinct (no duplicates); tuple order has no significance.

fields.Text: A relation whose cells each contain exactly one atomic value is said to be normalized, or in {{c1::First Normal Form (1NF)}}.
Tuple order has no significance because a relation is a {{c1::set}} (though records in a file always have a physical order).

fields.Back: Because a relation is a set, and a set has no repeated elements.

fields.Front: Why must all values in a column come from the same domain?
fields.Back: Because in a mathematical relation the possible values at a position are determined by the domain on which that position is defined.

fields.Front: Are mathematical relations normalized? Are relational-model relations?
fields.Back: Mathematical relations are not necessarily normalized; Codd chose relations in the relational model to be normalized (atomic cells).

fields.Front: Two tables both named EMPLOYEE in one database: what property is violated?
THINGY_TABLE has rows (Apple,Dog,77),(Orange,Cat,77),(Apple,Dog,77),(Orange,Pig,77): what is wrong?
fields.Back: Duplicate tuples (rows 1 and 3); tuples must be distinct.

fields.Text: Two tables with the same rows listed in a different order are {{c1::the same relation}}, because tuple order has no significance.

fields.Front: Two tables have the same rows but columns in a different order (YThingy, XThingy, ZThingy vs XThingy, YThingy, ZThingy): same relation?
fields.Back: Yes; attribute order has no significance.

fields.Front: A table has columns YThingy, XThingy, YThingy: what is wrong?
fields.Back: Duplicate attribute name; attribute names within a table must be unique.

fields.Front: DEPARTMENT has Location values 'NCB, WSC' and 'BG, NCB': what is wrong?
fields.Back: Cells are not atomic (two values in one cell), violating first normal form; a multi-valued attribute needs its own table.

fields.Front: Annotated EMPLOYEE table (SSN, FirstName, LastName, Department, Position; Laura Reid, Bob Bryan, Sylvia Osborn, Bob Bryan): how many tuples, attributes, and what is the key and SSN domain?
fields.Back: 4 tuples; 5 attributes; key SSN; sample domain of SSN is 000 to 999.

fields.Front: Two rows for 'Bob Bryan' (SSN 005 and 137) in the EMPLOYEE table: is this a problem?
fields.Back: No; the tuples differ in SSN, so they are distinct.

fields.Front: What is a cell, according to the instructor?
fields.Back: Where a row (tuple) and a column (attribute) meet; it may contain only one atomic value, not ten values separated by commas.

fields.Front: Give the instructor's phone-number example for the 'same domain' property.
fields.Back: If tuple 1 stores a 10-digit phone number, tuple 17 must also store a 10-digit value; you cannot have some tuples store numbers and others store letters for the same attribute.

fields.Text: Attribute order has no significance, but the norm is to put the {{c1::key}} first (EmpID or StudentNum before the names).

fields.Front: When might duplicate rows or a particular row order appear in practice, and what is the theoretical rule?
fields.Back: A query may return the same row twice, results may be displayed alphabetically, and rows may be stored on disk in an order for efficiency; in Codd's theory, tuples are never duplicated and order has no meaning.

fields.Text: Two tables both named EMPLOYEE (say full-time and part-time staff) in one database violate the {{c1::unique relation name}} property, even though their SSNs differ.

fields.Front: Why does the instructor say duplicate rows mean 'the key isn't working'?
fields.Back: A key is supposed to force every row to be unique; if two identical rows exist, no attribute set is doing that job.

fields.Front: Two columns are both named YThingy but have different domains. Is the relation valid?
fields.Back: No. Attribute names within a table must be unique regardless of domain.

fields.Text: A table with more than one value in a cell (e.g. Location = 'NCB, WSC') is not in {{c1::first normal form}}, which Codd's model requires.
